subject: Amply demo — model shortlist, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Reilly <sam@amply.io>, Nina Patel <nina@amply.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Amply demo recap — immediate model recommendations and next steps

Hi Sam / Nina,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciate you walking us through the ingestion and query patterns (batch CSV imports + low-latency interactive search). I promised a short follow-up with the initial model shortlist, why each fits Amply's constraints, and concrete next steps for an eval. High level notes from the call:

- Query pattern: 60% short-query intent paraphrase, 30% longer summarization of uploaded docs, 10% multi-turn clarifying.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for interactive queries.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-stage startup; prefer model choices that keep hosted per-token cost predictable.
- Quality tolerance: acceptable minor extractive drift on summaries, but hallucination score must be < 3% on our eval set.

Recommended shortlist (fast follow):
1) redwood-qa-13b-fp16 (balanced) — Rationale: lowest quality/latency sweet spot for your mix (strong paraphrase accuracy, good on concise summaries). Expect p95 latency ~220–300ms on our standard dedicated profile; per-1k tokens cost estimated in attached spreadsheet.
2) gemini-lite-Variant-A (quantized) — Rationale: cost-optimized option with acceptable degradation on longer summarization; strong at short intents. Lower token cost but higher variance on multi-turn.
3) open-mistral-30b-q4 (high-quality) — Rationale: highest fidelity for summaries; higher cost and latency (p95 ~420ms) — recommend as fallback for critical/paid-tier routes.

Concerns / regression flags to watch during eval:
- Summarization length drift: redwood-qa-13b tends to abbreviate long docs; we'll provide prompt set variations.
- Numeric stability: open-mistral-30b performs better but at cost.
- Caching and prefix reuse: throughput gains are possible with our cache config; we will include a suggested config.

Attachments and links: demo deck (amply-demo-deck.pdf), prompt set v1 (prompt-set-v1.csv), latency & cost estimates (latency-cost-estimates.xlsx). Public benchmark snapshot and the eval harness are here: https://redwood-inference.app/benchmarks/amply/20270312

Proposed next steps (mutual action plan):
- Week 0 (this week): We share the prompt set and baseline eval harness (attached).
- Week 1: You run a 3-day smoke test on a representative subset (we can run it for you if you prefer).
- Week 2: Joint review of failures + pick one model to pilot (can be dedicated capacity or hosted).

Ask: Can you confirm who on your side will own running the smoke tests? If you prefer, our solutions engineering team (Marissa and Karthik on cc) can run the first pass and share results.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your preference and will queue the bench run once we confirm the test owner.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0119

From: Sam Reilly <sam@amply.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Patel <nina@amply.io>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Amply demo — model shortlist, benchmarks, and next steps

Thanks Hannah — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifying questions before we agree to the smoke test: 

1) For redwood-qa-13b-fp16, you listed p95 ~220–300ms. Is that for a cold KV-cache or warm (typical of our interactive traffic)? Also, what GPU profile was used to estimate that?
2) For open-mistral-30b-q4, the p95 ~420ms is above our SLO — would you recommend routing critical calls to a dedicated instance with higher compute or doing an async fallback?
3) What are the expected token costs per 1k tokens for each shortlist model (hosted pricing) — I see the spreadsheet but could you paste the per-1k summary inline?

We prefer Redwood to run the first smoke test if you can — saves time for our eng. If Marissa/Karthik can own that, great. Also curious if you have a recommended prompt variant to reduce hallucination on summaries — last time our internal model hallucinated dates and small facts.

On ownership: I’ll cc Eng lead after we lock the test plan.

—Sam
Head of Product | Amply Analytics
sam@amply.io

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Reilly <sam@amply.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Nina Patel <nina@amply.io>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Amply demo — model shortlist, benchmarks, and next steps

Sam — great questions. Quick answers inline and a concrete plan to run the smoke test on our side this week.

1) Latency profiles: the 220–300ms p95 for redwood-qa-13b-fp16 assumes a warm KV/cache and our standard dedicated "d-high" profile (A100-class equivalent with 48GB). Cold-first-token is ~450ms; subsequent tokens drop significantly with the cache warmed. If you expect mostly interactive repeat queries, warm numbers are realistic. Full test config is in the attached spreadsheet and the public bench link: https://redwood-inference.app/benchmarks/amply/20270312 (see "latency_config" section).

2) For open-mistral-30b-q4: routing strategies we recommend:
- Dedicated upscale (higher vGPU) for paid-tier/critical queries (keeps p95 ~260–300ms)
- Or async fallback: serve initial concise answer via redwood-qa-13b, then re-rank/enrich with mistral in the background for persisted results. The right choice depends on SLA-criticality vs cost — happy to model both.

3) Per-1k token hosted pricing (summary):
- redwood-qa-13b-fp16: $1.20 / 1k tokens
- gemini-lite-Variant-A (q4): $0.55 / 1k tokens
- open-mistral-30b-q4: $2.75 / 1k tokens
(see latency-cost-estimates.xlsx for assumptions: tokenization ratio, avg response length, and our reserved vs hosted delta).

Hallucination / prompt recommendations: attach prompt-set-v1.csv contains three variants. Our recommended pattern to reduce factual drift on summaries: instructive system prompt + explicit grounding block and a short citation policy ("If not found, state 'no evidence' and list sources"). Example snippet from the prompt set: 

"System: You are a concise summarizer that only uses the provided documents. If a fact cannot be verified in the documents, do not invent it — respond 'no evidence'. Keep answers under 120 words unless asked."

We will run the 3-day smoke test on our infra (Marissa / Karthik will run). Plan:
- Today: we kick off bench-run with your sample dataset (please upload one representative CSV to the shared Drive link or reply with S3 path).
- Day 1: baseline runs for all three models (latency + hallucination metrics).
- Day 2: run two prompt variants + caching on redwood-qa-13b to measure stability.
- Day 3: aggregated report + recommended pilot model and routing strategy.

Deliverables we will share:
- Bench report (CSV + dashboard link)
- Failure list with example prompts that hallucinated
- Cost estimate by projected monthly tokens (3 scenarios: 10k, 100k, 1M monthly queries)

Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm you can start the run today if Sam replies with the data path?

Sam — if you can drop a short sample (10–20 docs) to the shared Drive or give us an S3 path, we’ll queue the job. If you prefer we can take a masked sample.

Thanks — will follow up with the bench link when the run starts.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah@redwood.ai
